# Third-party dataset: `AxBench` (Concept500)

Labelled concept-steering data from
[*AxBench: Steering LLMs? Even Simple Baselines Outperform Sparse
Autoencoders*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.17148) (Wu, Arora, Geiger, Wang,
Huang, Jurafsky, Manning, Potts — 2025).

- **Source:** https://huggingface.co/datasets/pyvene/axbench-concept500
- **License:** CC-BY-4.0 (see the HF dataset card). Redistributed here only by
  reference — fetched on demand, **not committed**.
- **Pinned commit:** `manifest.json` (`source_commit` `ad8a5d60…`, last modified
  2025-01-24), per `docs/PREREG.md` §3b.

## What this is, in this repo

AxBench is the benchmark behind the FK-5 boundary check
(`docs/work-splits/fk-task-list.md`): run **our** difference-of-means steering on
it and measure how well single-direction additive steering actually controls a
target concept. Its own headline is that a plain **prompting** baseline and
**DiffMean** (difference of means — our method) both beat SAEs, so it is the
natural place to see where our single direction holds up and where it breaks.

Concept500 is organised **per concept**: for each of ~500 concepts it holds
labelled `positive` (the response expresses the concept) and `negative` (the
unsteered response) instruction/response pairs — exactly the contrast DiffMean is
built from.

### Columns (HF schema)

| Column | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `input` | the instruction / user prompt |
| `output` | the response (concept-bearing if `category == positive`) |
| `category` | **`positive`** (concept present) or **`negative`** (unsteered) — the DiffMean contrast |
| `output_concept` | the concept text (`EEEEE` = no concept, i.e. negatives) |
| `concept_id` | globally unique concept id (matches the released dictionary's subspace index) |
| `concept_genre` | `text` / `code` / `math` |

The `axbench` loader (`src/bias_steer/datasets.py`) maps `input` →
`Example.prompt` and stashes the rest in `metadata`: `label = category`
(positive/negative — the extraction contrast), `category = concept_genre`
(the coarse stratify key), plus `concept_id`, `output_concept`, and the reference
`output`. Filter to one concept with `SampleSpec(filter={"concept_id": [...]})`.

### Variants (which released copy to read)

AxBench shipped one copy of Concept500 per (extraction model, layer) it released
dictionaries for — `2b/l10`, `2b/l20` (gemma-2-2b-it) and `9b/l20`, `9b/l31`
(gemma-2-9b-it). **We extract on our own model**, so the folder only picks which
released copy of the labelled text to read; the default is `2b/l20`. (The
reference `output` text was generated by the AxBench pipeline, not by our model —
relevant if you capture residuals on the provided outputs rather than on freshly
generated ones.)

## How to fetch

```bash
python scripts/fetch_axbench.py                     # 2b/l20 train+test (default)
python scripts/fetch_axbench.py --variant 9b/l31    # a different released copy
python scripts/fetch_axbench.py --force             # re-download
```

Files land under `third_party/axbench/` (git-ignored). Reading them needs
`pandas` (already a project dependency); the fetcher is stdlib-only.
